messages:
Priya (AE): Heads up — ACME POC in panic. Users not appearing in app, SSO intermittently 401/invalid assertion. Exec demo tomorrow AM. Can we triage now?
Lila (Solutions Eng): What does the SCIM call return? 401 vs 403 different root causes.
ACME (IdP Admin): SCIM calls from Okta to https://scim.redwood.ai/orgs/acme return `401 Unauthorized` with body: '{\"error\":\"invalid_token\"}'. Our team used the API key generated from the hosted console.
Tom S. (SE): Hosted keys differ by org type. On Dedicated/Private onboarding we require a scoped SCIM service key created under admin settings. If they used a short-lived user key it won't work.
Priya (AE): ACME is switching between Hosted and a dedicated pool for POC. Could that explain the mismatch?
Tom S. (SE): Yes — token audience differs for dedicated endpoints. Quick fix: generate a tenant-scoped SCIM service key and set it in Okta's provisioning (serviceAccount token).
DevEx Bot: Admin action: POST /admin/tenants/ACME/keys {type: "service_scim", scopes:["scim:read","scim:write"], ttl:86400} -> `key_id: sk-temp-acme-20260401` (delivered to Lila).
Lila (Solutions Eng): Created sk-temp-acme-20260401 and updated Okta. SCIM now returns 200 for user create. Group sync still reporting 409 duplicate on `externalId:okta:group:eng-123`.
Tom S. (SE): 409 = group exists locally. Our SCIM handler rejects duplicate externalId by default. We can switch tenant-specific behavior to "attach_existing_on_match" so Okta groups map to existing groups if names align.
Priya (AE): ACME already had groups created manually named exactly 'eng-team' and 'ml-platform'. Please link not duplicate.
Tom S. (SE): I'll enable `scim.attach_on_name=true` for tenant ACME. Deploying to canary nodes.
DevEx Bot: Feature toggle `scim.attach_on_name=true` applied to tenant ACME. Canary nodes: rdw-hosted-02.
ACME (IdP Admin): Separately, SAML is flakey. Our default NameID format is email, but your SP expects persistent ID. Users sometimes get "NameID format not supported".
Tom S. (SE): We prefer persistent but for a POC we can accept email as fallback if tenant sets `saml.allow_email_nameid=true`. That will perform matching by email claim and log events.
Security (SOC): We can allow email fallback for 12 hours max for demo, must enable audit logging and notify security ops.
Lila (Solutions Eng): Enabled `saml.allow_email_nameid=true` for ACME for 12h and turned on extended audit logs. Also added an event hook to alert on mismatches.
ACME (IdP Admin): After that change, 95% of users can SSO. One engineer still blocked with "subject missing". We found their Okta assertion omitted `email` claim for that user.
Tom S. (SE): If email missing we can't match. Workaround: manual invite or fix IdP mapping. For POC, we can provision that account via SCIM as admin.
Priya (AE): Can we create temporary support access for ACME SREs to debug tomorrow? Prefer limited TTL.
Tom S. (SE): I'll create a support key `sk-support-acme-20260401` with scopes `scim:read scim:write iam:impersonate` and TTL 8h. I'll send via secure 1:1.
DevEx Bot: Support key created and sent to Lila via encrypted message. Key ID: sk-support-acme-20260401.
Security (SOC): Approve temporary keys for support with TTL < 24h. Must schedule automated revoke and create rollback runbook.
Lila (Solutions Eng): Tests now: user provisioning OK, groups linked, SSO passes for testers. Demo prep call scheduled for 09:00 tomorrow. I'll note rollback at 20:00 tomorrow to reset `scim.attach_on_name` and `saml.allow_email_nameid`.
Priya (AE): Thanks all. Please post final verification in this thread when rollback scheduled. Also capture steps for ACME runbook so they avoid this during production onboarding.
Tom S. (SE): Will document and add to onboarding checklist: 1) create tenant-scoped SCIM service key; 2) verify NameID format or enable email fallback temporarily; 3) pre-seed groups to avoid dedupe collisions.
ACME (IdP Admin): Appreciate the fast turnaround. Looking forward to tomorrow's demo. :rocket:
